notes.body: assigned to @pquantin
LGFM
Running out of time for today, I will try to review it tomorrow.
this should be enum mbim_extended_version_vals mbim_extended_version

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/177/diffs?diff_id=111474706&start_sha=cf1698f5dee4ddea712030627337570912a1f998#3f4c602f6670690382c1b302509061e51de0a1de_961_961)
As discussed in the previous patch set, the MBIM prefix should be dropped IMHO. Maybe use "Frequency Range Unknown" instead?

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/177/diffs?diff_id=111474706&start_sha=cf1698f5dee4ddea712030627337570912a1f998#3f4c602f6670690382c1b302509061e51de0a1de_1515_1515)
Presumably you should display a range rather than 'less than". See nr_rrc_RSRP_Range_fmt() in packet-nr-rrc.c

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/177/diffs?diff_id=111474706&start_sha=cf1698f5dee4ddea712030627337570912a1f998#3f4c602f6670690382c1b302509061e51de0a1de_2425_2424)
Presumably you should display a range rather than 'less than". See nr_rrc_SINR_Range_fmt() in packet-nr-rrc.c

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/177/diffs?diff_id=111474706&start_sha=cf1698f5dee4ddea712030627337570912a1f998#3f4c602f6670690382c1b302509061e51de0a1de_2439_2438)
It should be ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN. Moreover the notation is with a dot (1.0, 2.0) so you might want to use a custom display.

MBIM extensions Release number of the sender in BCD, with implied decimal point between bits 7 and 8.  0x0100 == 1.00 == 1.0.  This is a little-endian constant, so the bytes will be 0x00, 0x01. With `ENC_BIG_ENDIAN`, it will return 1 or 2 which is the right number. With ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN, it has to MOD of 256

No this is wrong. As explained in Microsoft documentation, the version here is 1.0, not 1. And you can prettify the output by using a custom display as explained previously. If a version 3.1 is introduced later on your display will be invalid also. With ENC_BIG_ENDIAN it works by chance currently.
OK. Will do a little more to display the full decimal

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/177/diffs?diff_id=111474706&start_sha=cf1698f5dee4ddea712030627337570912a1f998#3f4c602f6670690382c1b302509061e51de0a1de_5190_5196)
It should be ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN. Moreover the notation is with a dot (1.0, 2.0) so you might want to use a custom display.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/177/diffs?diff_id=111474706&start_sha=cf1698f5dee4ddea712030627337570912a1f998#3f4c602f6670690382c1b302509061e51de0a1de_5192_5198)
You need to change the bitmask to `0x0000ff80`

Why 0x0000ff80? 
`0x00000040` is the right mask for 5G
I'm talking about the `hf_mbim_data_class_reserved_gsm` field, not the `hf_mbim_data_class_5g` one. Now there is one bit less as reserved.
I see.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/177/diffs?diff_id=111474706&start_sha=cf1698f5dee4ddea712030627337570912a1f998#3f4c602f6670690382c1b302509061e51de0a1de_7928_7945)
You can also use your `mbim_rsrp_signal_state_fmt` function
`RSRP Threshold` is a absolute number in dBm, so I think it cannot use mbim_rsrp_signal_state_fmt like "rssi threshold"
Then add a custom function to display the value in dBm

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/177/diffs?diff_id=111474706&start_sha=cf1698f5dee4ddea712030627337570912a1f998#3f4c602f6670690382c1b302509061e51de0a1de_8532_8549)

OK after double checking the Microsoft documentation, I see that I misinterpreted the meaning of this field (in 3GPP specification the threshold has another meaning, thus my mistake). Sorry about that.
FYI you can have dBm / dB appended automatically after the value using

`        { &hf_mbim_signal_state_element_snr_threshold,
            { "SNR Threshold", "mbim.control.signal_state_element.snr_threshold",
               FT_UINT32, BASE_DEC|BASE_UNIT_STRING, &units_dbm, 0,
              NULL, HFILL }
        },
`

and by including unit_strings.h. But I'm also fine with your cahnge, let me know what you prefer.
will update as you suggested
You can also use your `mbim_snr_signal_state_fmt` function
`SNR Threshold` is a absolute number in dB, so I think it cannot use `mbim_snr_signal_state_fmt` like "rssi threshold"
Then add a custom function to display the value in dB
Is it ok to just update hf name to "SNR Threshold in dB"? I don't see too much value to just append dB after the number.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/177/diffs?diff_id=111474706&start_sha=cf1698f5dee4ddea712030627337570912a1f998#3f4c602f6670690382c1b302509061e51de0a1de_8537_8554)
That's not what I meant,sorry for the misunderstanding. I lean that you should display the real value like what you do for the range.
See my comment above, there is also units_decibels
fixed
If the text for the description is the same as the title, you can use NULL for the fourth parameter
